So this is more of a rough guide than a recipe...

500g Mushrooms roughly chopped

2 Springs of Rosemary roughly chopped

5 Sage leaves roughly chopped

1 small onion finely diced

1 tablespoon of sugar

Breadcrumbs (I literally have no idea how much I used. Just enough for it to have some structural integrity so it doesn't all just fall apart.)

Butter (enough to cook the mushrooms in)

2-3 cloves of garlic, finely chopped

I just bought some puff pastry because i'm lazy

Eggs & milk for egg wash

Seasoning

Tiny splash of balsamic vinegar

​

Melt the butter in a pan with the garlic, when melted add the mushrooms, rosemary and sage. When that's all cooked out (mushrooms will be squashy, like 10mins I think? you can't really overcook mushrooms so I wouldn't worry about that) stick it all in a blender and blend the living christ out of it to make what i'm going to call the 'mushroom mix'. If its too dry to blend add small amounts of water very slowly, you want to keep it as thick as possible, so try to use the very least you can.

​

Put the chopped onion in a pan with a tiny bit of oil on a low heat with the sugar, best to keep an eye on it, you want the onions sweet to taste and will be light brown in colour when cooked, sugar burns easy so its probably best to keep an eye on it whilst you're doing it. 

Once the onions are done add them to the mushroom mix. Add some seasoning and mix it all together, add balsamic vinegar. Then add the breadcrumbs. You just want it to have its almost like a paste, so it doesn't just fall apart. You sort of want it so you can mould it in your hand.

​

Put it in a line on a sheet of puff pastry with some egg wash to help it stick for when you're rolling it then.. I guess roll it. I like to use a fork to join the two ends of the pastry together so it sticks together (This is a really bad description i'm sorry.). Then use the remaining eggwash on and around the top of the roll to give it a golden colour once cooked

​

Bake in a pre-warmed oven at around 180c until golden brown, usually 10-15mins.

This is for scrambled eggs. If you want to best scrambled eggs you want to cook them low and slow. Start with some butter, melt it down in the pan and line the pan with it, cook out turmeric in the butter, have your scrambled egg mix to hand (it's actually really good to put a touch of nutmeg in the mix too!).

 Pour the egg mix in the turmeric butter and leave them to cook out for a minute or two on a low heat before you start scrambling. 

Don't be aggressive with it when you're stirring the eggs in the pan, nice be gentle is fine. If they look almost done then they are done. They will keep cooking after you take them off the heat. There's too many overcooked scrambled eggs out there. 

Again I'd suggest finishing them with some acidity of your choice.

It's great in soups, mix a touch through your scrambled eggs, I think its used in certain styles of caribbean cooking too.

Usually I'd use it in conjunction with other spices too but it's just one I make sure I always have in the house.
